fix.notes: The fix only affects the code path where a card name in the rotation cache table has no corresponding oracle entry. In normal operation this never fires; during the brief post-release window before the oracle is updated it prevents a KeyError crash and logs a warning instead. No schema changes, no DB migrations needed.
fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

`load_rotation()` in `decksite/data/rotation.py` called `cards[c.name]` (line 41) to look up each rotation card in the oracle dictionary. If a card name from the `_rotation` table was not yet present in the oracle (which happens in the window between a set release and the oracle DB being updated), this raised a `KeyError` and crashed the entire rotation page load.

## What changed

Replaced the direct dictionary access with `cards.get(c.name)`. If the lookup returns `None` (card not in oracle), the card container is left without oracle fields and a `logger.warning` is emitted. This matches the graceful-degradation intent the surrounding `try/except DatabaseException` block already establishes.

**Diff:** 1 file, +5 / -1 lines, all in `decksite/data/rotation.py`.

## Validation

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (all checks).
- `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 845 passed, 1 skipped, 89 deselected. MariaDB was available in the test environment so the full suite including DB-dependent tests ran successfully.

Fixes #12299
